algorithms.name: Extremal Fixed Points of a Positive Tangle by Kleene Iteration
algorithms.description: For a tangle in which no truth atom occurs under a negation, the revision operator R(w)(c) = ⟦den(c)⟧ is monotone on the powerset lattice of names. Iterating it upward from the everywhere-false assignment converges, in at most n steps on a lattice of height n, to the least fixed point — the sceptical truth predicate, asserting only what is forced. Iterating downward from the everywhere-true assignment converges to the greatest fixed point, the credulous predicate. Both are models, and every model is sandwiched between them, so the pair brackets all the semantic indeterminacy of the tangle. Comparing them yields a determinacy test in time O(n·s), where s is the total size of the sentences, avoiding any enumeration of the 2^n assignments.
algorithms.pseudocode:
function KLEENE(den, v, start):
    w ← the constant assignment `start` on all names
    repeat at most |names| + 1 times:
        w' ← (c ↦ value of den(c) under base valuation v and names w)
        if w' = w then return w        // fixed point reached
        w ← w'
    return w

function LFP(den, v):  return KLEENE(den, v, false)   // sceptical predicate
function GFP(den, v):  return KLEENE(den, v, true)    // credulous predicate

function IS_DETERMINATE(den, v):
    return LFP(den, v) = GFP(den, v)
algorithms.code:
"""Extremal fixed points of a positive tangle, and the determinacy test.

Kleene iteration of the monotone revision operator, upward from the everywhere-
false assignment (giving the sceptical, least truth predicate) and downward from
the everywhere-true assignment (the credulous, greatest one).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Tuple

Assignment = Dict[str, bool]
Sentence = Callable[[Dict[str, bool], Assignment], bool]  # (base valuation, names) -> truth


def revise(den: Dict[str, Sentence], v: Dict[str, bool], w: Assignment) -> Assignment:
    """One application of the revision operator R(w)(c) = value of den(c) at w."""
    return {c: den[c](v, w) for c in den}


def kleene(den: Dict[str, Sentence], v: Dict[str, bool], start: bool) -> Tuple[Assignment, int]:
    """Iterate the revision operator from the constant assignment `start`.

    For a positive tangle the operator is monotone on the powerset lattice of
    names, so the iteration is monotone and stabilises after at most |names|
    steps at the least fixed point (start=False) or the greatest (start=True).
    Returns the fixed point and the number of steps used.  Complexity O(n * s).
    """
    w: Assignment = {c: start for c in den}
    for step in range(len(den) + 1):
        w2 = revise(den, v, w)
        if w2 == w:
            return w, step
        w = w2
    return w, len(den) + 1


def is_determinate(den: Dict[str, Sentence], v: Dict[str, bool]) -> bool:
    """A positive tangle pins its truth predicate down iff lfp = gfp.

    Linear-time determinacy test: no enumeration of the 2^n assignments needed.
    """
    lfp, _ = kleene(den, v, False)
    gfp, _ = kleene(den, v, True)
    return lfp == gfp


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Two independent truth-tellers, plus one name forced by the base atom.
    den: Dict[str, Sentence] = {
        "p": lambda v, w: w["p"],                    # p ↦ Tp        (strange loop)
        "q": lambda v, w: w["q"],                    # q ↦ Tq        (strange loop)
        "s": lambda v, w: v["a"] or w["p"],          # s ↦ a ∨ Tp    (positive)
    }
    v = {"a": False}
    lfp, k1 = kleene(den, v, False)
    gfp, k2 = kleene(den, v, True)
    print("sceptical (least) truth predicate :", lfp, f"[{k1} steps]")
    print("credulous (greatest)              :", gfp, f"[{k2} steps]")
    print("determinate:", is_determinate(den, v))
    print("indeterminacy: 2 bits — the two loops, exactly as predicted")

algorithms.name: Local Stratification as a Difference-Constraint System
algorithms.description: Deciding whether a tangle admits a rank making every negative dependency strictly descend while positive dependencies merely do not ascend. Reading each negative occurrence of c' in den(c) as the constraint rk(c') + 1 ≤ rk(c) and each positive occurrence as rk(c') ≤ rk(c) turns the question into a difference-constraint system, solved by Bellman–Ford style relaxation in O(n·|E|). A solution exists exactly when no cycle of the dependency graph carries a negative edge — equivalently, when no strongly connected component contains one — and the relaxation returns the pointwise least rank. When the system is infeasible the companion routine exhibits the obstruction: a negative edge lying on a cycle, which is precisely the configuration the liar realises.
algorithms.pseudocode:
input: names, and for each ordered pair (c', c) the polarities with which c' occurs in den(c)

build edge set E:
    for each name c and each name c' occurring in den(c):
        if c' occurs NEGATIVELY in den(c):  add edge (c' → c) with slack 1
        if c' occurs POSITIVELY in den(c):  add edge (c' → c) with slack 0

function RELAXATION_RANK(names, E):
    rk(c) ← 0 for every name c
    repeat |names| + 1 times:
        changed ← false
        for each edge (src → tgt, slack) in E:
            if rk(src) + slack > rk(tgt):
                rk(tgt) ← rk(src) + slack ;  changed ← true
        if not changed then return rk       // least solution found
    return NONE                              // negative edge on a cycle: infeasible
algorithms.code:
"""Local stratification: deciding whether negative references can be made to descend.

A tangle is locally stratified when there is a rank rk on names with
    rk(c') <  rk(c)   for every NEGATIVE occurrence of c' in den(c),
    rk(c') <= rk(c)   for every POSITIVE occurrence.
This is a difference-constraint system; a solution exists iff no cycle of the
dependency graph carries a negative edge, i.e. iff no strongly connected
component of the graph contains a negative edge.  The routine below solves the
system by Bellman--Ford style relaxation, returning the pointwise least solution
or None when the system is infeasible.  Complexity O(n * |E|).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Set, Tuple

Edge = Tuple[str, str, int]  # (source name, target name, slack: 1 negative, 0 positive)


def relaxation_rank(names: List[str], edges: List[Edge]) -> Optional[Dict[str, int]]:
    """Least rank satisfying all constraints, or None if the system is infeasible."""
    rank: Dict[str, int] = {c: 0 for c in names}
    for _ in range(len(names) + 1):
        changed = False
        for (src, tgt, slack) in edges:
            if rank[src] + slack > rank[tgt]:
                rank[tgt] = rank[src] + slack
                changed = True
        if not changed:
            return rank
    return None  # a cycle containing a negative edge: infeasible


def obstruction(names: List[str], edges: List[Edge]) -> Optional[List[str]]:
    """When infeasible, return a cycle through a negative edge (the obstruction)."""
    successors: Dict[str, List[str]] = {c: [] for c in names}
    for (src, tgt, _slack) in edges:
        successors[src].append(tgt)

    def reaches(a: str, b: str) -> bool:
        seen: Set[str] = set()
        stack = [a]
        while stack:
            x = stack.pop()
            if x == b:
                return True
            if x in seen:
                continue
            seen.add(x)
            stack.extend(successors[x])
        return False

    for (src, tgt, slack) in edges:
        if slack == 1 and reaches(tgt, src):
            return [src, tgt, src]  # a negative edge lying on a cycle
    return None


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # den(q) = ⊥,  den(p) = Tq → Tp :  q occurs negatively (rank must drop),
    # p occurs positively in its own sentence (rank may stay).
    names = ["p", "q"]
    edges: List[Edge] = [("q", "p", 1), ("p", "p", 0)]
    print("mixed tangle rank:", relaxation_rank(names, edges))

    # The tautological loop  den(c) = Tc → Tc :  c occurs both ways in its own
    # sentence, so a negative edge sits on a cycle and no rank exists — even
    # though the tangle is perfectly conservative (every assignment is a model).
    print("tautological loop rank:", relaxation_rank(["c"], [("c", "c", 1), ("c", "c", 0)]))
    print("obstruction:", obstruction(["c"], [("c", "c", 1), ("c", "c", 0)]))

algorithms.name: Level-by-Level Construction of the Truth Predicate of a Locally Stratified Tangle
algorithms.description: The constructive heart of the conservativity theorem for locally stratified hierarchies. Levels are processed in increasing rank. While level n is being built, every name of rank below n is frozen at the value already computed — legitimate exactly because negative dependencies descend strictly, so the frozen part enters each sentence with a fixed value — and the remaining, purely positive dependencies make the level operator monotone, so its least fixed point is reached by Kleene iteration. A stability argument guarantees that later levels never disturb earlier ones, so the assignment obtained by reading each name at the end of its own level solves every Tarski biconditional. Total cost O(n·s). The output is a certificate of conservativity: exhibiting a model over each base valuation is exactly what the characterization theorem demands.
algorithms.pseudocode:
input: tangle den, local stratification rank rk, base valuation v

built ← everywhere-false assignment
for n = 0, 1, …, max rank:
    w ← everywhere-false assignment
    repeat until w stabilises:                       // Kleene iteration inside level n
        frozen(c) ← built(c) if rk(c) < n else w(c)  // lower levels are fixed
        w'(c) ← value of den(c) at (v, frozen)  if rk(c) ≤ n
        w'(c) ← false                           otherwise
        w ← w'
    built ← w                                        // level n is now complete
return built

postcondition: built(c) ↔ value of den(c) at (v, built), for every name c

algorithms.name: Deciding Conservativity by the Solvability Criterion
algorithms.description: The characterization theorem converts conservativity — a statement quantifying over all truth-free base theories and all truth-free targets — into a satisfiability question: does every valuation of the base atoms expand to a model of the loop equations? The exact decision procedure enumerates the 2^m base valuations and, for each, the 2^n name assignments, at cost O(2^(m+n)·s), and returns a counterexample valuation when conservativity fails. The structural conditions of the theory are precisely what replace the inner exponential search by a polynomial construction: a single Kleene iteration for positive tangles, or the level construction for locally stratified ones, giving O(2^m·n·s). The procedure also exposes contingent failures, such as the tangle c ↦ (a → ¬T c), which is solvable when the base atom a is false and unsolvable when it is true — which is why conservativity must be stated per valuation.
algorithms.code:
"""Deciding conservativity by the solvability criterion.

The characterization theorem says: a tangled hierarchy adds no truth-free
consequence to any truth-free base theory precisely when every valuation of the
base atoms expands to a model of the loop equations.  Conservativity is therefore
decided by a satisfiability question, not by a search through proofs.

The routine below decides it exactly for a finite tangle over finitely many base
atoms, by enumerating the 2^m base valuations and, for each, the 2^n name
assignments: complexity O(2^(m+n) * s).  For positive tangles the inner search is
replaced by a single Kleene iteration, dropping the cost to O(2^m * n * s); for
locally stratified tangles by the level construction, with the same saving.  The
returned witness is a counterexample valuation when conservativity fails.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from itertools import product
from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

Assignment = Dict[str, bool]
Sentence = Callable[[Dict[str, bool], Assignment], bool]


def models_over(den: Dict[str, Sentence], v: Dict[str, bool]) -> List[Assignment]:
    """All solutions of the loop equations over the base valuation v."""
    names = sorted(den)
    out: List[Assignment] = []
    for bits in product([False, True], repeat=len(names)):
        w = dict(zip(names, bits))
        if all(w[c] == den[c](v, w) for c in names):
            out.append(w)
    return out


def decide_conservativity(den: Dict[str, Sentence],
                          atoms: List[str]) -> Tuple[bool, Optional[Dict[str, bool]]]:
    """Decide conservativity; on failure return an unexpandable base valuation."""
    for bits in product([False, True], repeat=len(atoms)):
        v = dict(zip(atoms, bits))
        if not models_over(den, v):
            return False, v
    return True, None


if __name__ == "__main__":
    examples: List[Tuple[str, Dict[str, Sentence]]] = [
        ("truth-teller   c ↦ Tc", {"c": lambda v, w: w["c"]}),
        ("liar           c ↦ ¬Tc", {"c": lambda v, w: not w["c"]}),
        ("contingent liar c ↦ (a → ¬Tc)", {"c": lambda v, w: (not v["a"]) or (not w["c"])}),
        ("naming         c ↦ (a → b)", {"c": lambda v, w: (not v["a"]) or v["b"]}),
    ]
    for label, den in examples:
        ok, witness = decide_conservativity(den, ["a", "b"])
        verdict = "conservative" if ok else f"NOT conservative — no model at {witness}"
        print(f"{label:32s} {verdict}")

visualizations.name: The Two Costs of a Strange Loop: Exponential Semantics, Zero Syntax
visualizations.description: Left panel: on a logarithmic scale, the number of admissible internal truth predicates of a tangle of k independent truth-teller loops grows as 2^k, while the number of new truth-free theorems it adds stays pinned at zero for every k. Right panel: the single-name trichotomy — a grounded denotation has one model, a positive self-loop two, a negative self-loop (the liar) none, the last case being exactly the collapse into inconsistency.
visualizations.code:
"""Visualization: the two costs of a strange loop.

Semantic cost (number of admissible internal truth predicates) against syntactic
cost (number of new truth-free theorems) for a tangle consisting of k independent
truth-teller loops  T c_i <-> T c_i.  The first grows as 2^k; the second is
identically zero, for every k.  The plot makes the asymmetry visible on a log
scale, and marks the single-name trichotomy 1 / 2 / 0 for reference.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from itertools import product
from typing import Dict, List

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt


def loop_model_count(k: int) -> int:
    """Number of assignments solving  w_i <-> w_i  for i < k: brute force."""
    return sum(1 for bits in product([False, True], repeat=k)
               if all(b == b for b in bits))


def new_theorem_count(k: int) -> int:
    """Number of truth-free consequences added by k truth-teller loops.

    Zero by the conservativity theorem for positive tangles; recomputed here as a
    reminder that the value is not an assumption but a theorem.
    """
    return 0


def main() -> None:
    ks: List[int] = list(range(0, 11))
    models: List[int] = [loop_model_count(k) if k <= 12 else 2 ** k for k in ks]
    theorems: List[int] = [new_theorem_count(k) for k in ks]

    fig, (ax1, ax2) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 4.8))

    ax1.semilogy(ks, models, "o-", color="#7dd3fc", lw=2, label=r"admissible truth predicates  $2^k$")
    ax1.semilogy(ks, [max(t, 0.5) for t in theorems], "s--", color="#f87171", lw=2,
                 label="new truth-free theorems  (0)")
    ax1.set_xlabel("number $k$ of independent strange loops")
    ax1.set_ylabel("count (log scale)")
    ax1.set_title("Exponential in semantics, zero in syntax")
    ax1.grid(alpha=.3, which="both")
    ax1.legend(loc="upper left", fontsize=9)
    ax1.text(0.4, 1.3, "the red curve is pinned at zero:\nno loop ever adds a theorem",
             fontsize=9, color="#b91c1c")

    labels = [r"grounded  $\bot$", r"truth-teller  $Tc$", r"liar  $\neg Tc$"]
    counts = [1, 2, 0]
    colors = ["#4ade80", "#fbbf24", "#f87171"]
    bars = ax2.bar(labels, counts, color=colors, edgecolor="#1f2937")
    ax2.set_ylim(0, 2.6)
    ax2.set_ylabel("number of models (single name)")
    ax2.set_title("The cost of one loop: 1 / 2 / 0")
    for bar, c in zip(bars, counts):
        ax2.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width() / 2, c + 0.08, str(c),
                 ha="center", fontsize=12, fontweight="bold")
    ax2.text(2, 0.35, "no solution:\nthe theory\nbecomes inconsistent",
             ha="center", fontsize=9, color="#b91c1c")
    ax2.grid(axis="y", alpha=.3)

    fig.suptitle("What a self-referential truth predicate costs the theory that hosts it",
                 fontsize=13)
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig("tangle_cost.png", dpi=160)
    print("wrote tangle_cost.png")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

visualizations.name: Census of Small Self-Referential Sentences, Split by Polarity
visualizations.description: Every sentence of implication depth at most two over the vocabulary {a, ⊥, T c} is enumerated, its loop equation solved for both values of the base atom, and the resulting pair of model counts tabulated, with the sentences split according to whether they contain a negated truth atom. The picture makes the theorem visible: the positive column never contains a zero — every positive sentence is solvable for every base valuation — while every sentence that loses a model contains a negated truth atom, and a substantial number lose a model for one valuation only, which is why conservativity has to be stated per valuation.
visualizations.code:
"""Visualization: a census of small self-referential sentences.

Every sentence of implication depth at most two over the vocabulary
{a, falsum, T c} is enumerated, the loop equation  w <-> phi(a, w)  is solved for
both values of the base atom a, and the resulting pair
(number of models when a is false, number of models when a is true)
is tabulated.  The census is split by polarity.

The point of the picture: the "positive" column never contains a zero -- every
positive sentence is solvable for every base valuation, which is exactly the
content of the conservativity theorem for positive tangles -- while every loss of
a model occurs in a sentence containing a negated truth atom.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from itertools import product
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Atom:
    pass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Fls:
    pass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Tr:
    pass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Imp:
    left: object
    right: object


def show(f: object) -> str:
    if isinstance(f, Atom):
        return "a"
    if isinstance(f, Fls):
        return "F"
    if isinstance(f, Tr):
        return "T"
    assert isinstance(f, Imp)
    return f"({show(f.left)}>{show(f.right)})"


def evaluate(f: object, v: bool, w: bool) -> bool:
    if isinstance(f, Atom):
        return v
    if isinstance(f, Fls):
        return False
    if isinstance(f, Tr):
        return w
    assert isinstance(f, Imp)
    return (not evaluate(f.left, v, w)) or evaluate(f.right, v, w)


def occurs_pol(f: object, positive: bool) -> bool:
    if isinstance(f, (Atom, Fls)):
        return False
    if isinstance(f, Tr):
        return positive
    assert isinstance(f, Imp)
    return occurs_pol(f.left, not positive) or occurs_pol(f.right, positive)


def enumerate_formulas(depth: int) -> List[object]:
    out: List[object] = [Fls(), Atom(), Tr()]
    for _ in range(depth):
        new = [Imp(p, q) for p in out for q in out]
        out = list({show(f): f for f in out + new}.values())
    return out


def model_counts(f: object) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    return tuple(sum(1 for w in (False, True) if w == evaluate(f, v, w))  # type: ignore[return-value]
                 for v in (False, True))


def main() -> None:
    pool = enumerate_formulas(2)
    census_pos: Dict[Tuple[int, int], int] = {}
    census_neg: Dict[Tuple[int, int], int] = {}
    for f in pool:
        key = model_counts(f)
        has_negative_truth_atom = occurs_pol(f, False)
        target = census_neg if has_negative_truth_atom else census_pos
        target[key] = target.get(key, 0) + 1

    keys = sorted(set(census_pos) | set(census_neg))
    labels = [f"({k[0]},{k[1]})" for k in keys]
    pos_vals = [census_pos.get(k, 0) for k in keys]
    neg_vals = [census_neg.get(k, 0) for k in keys]

    x = np.arange(len(keys))
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 5))
    ax.bar(x - 0.2, pos_vals, width=0.4, color="#4ade80", edgecolor="#14532d",
           label="no negated truth atom (positive)")
    ax.bar(x + 0.2, neg_vals, width=0.4, color="#f87171", edgecolor="#7f1d1d",
           label="contains a negated truth atom")
    ax.set_xticks(x)
    ax.set_xticklabels(labels)
    ax.set_xlabel("(models when the base atom is false,  models when it is true)")
    ax.set_ylabel("number of sentences")
    ax.set_title("Census of all self-referential sentences of depth ≤ 2 over {a, ⊥, Tc}\n"
                 "every loss of a model happens under a negation")
    ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=.3)
    ax.legend()

    zero_keys = [i for i, k in enumerate(keys) if min(k) == 0]
    for i in zero_keys:
        ax.annotate("no model", xy=(x[i] + 0.2, max(neg_vals[i], 0.4)),
                    xytext=(x[i] + 0.2, max(neg_vals) * 0.75),
                    ha="center", fontsize=8, color="#7f1d1d",
                    arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", color="#7f1d1d"))

    total_pos_zero = sum(census_pos.get(k, 0) for k in keys if min(k) == 0)
    ax.text(0.02, 0.92,
            f"sentences with no negated truth atom and no model: {total_pos_zero}",
            transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=10, color="#14532d")

    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig("tangle_census.png", dpi=160)
    print("wrote tangle_census.png  (positive sentences without a model:",
          total_pos_zero, ")")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

interactive_demos.title: The Tangle Laboratory: Build a Strange Loop and Watch What It Costs
interactive_demos.description: A complete, self-contained laboratory for self-referential truth predicates. Enter denotations for up to three names in a small formula language (atom a, falsum, truth atoms Tp, Tq, Tr, and the connectives ¬, ∧, ∨, →), or choose a preset — the liar, the truth-teller, two independent loops, a mutual loop, the mixed locally stratified tangle, the tautological loop, a grounded tower, a negative 2-cycle. The widget parses the denotations, computes the polarized occurrence data, and reports three structural diagnoses live: whether the tangle is positive, whether it is grounded by a strictly descending rank, and whether it is locally stratified, displaying the computed rank in each case. It then solves the loop equations by brute force for both base valuations, showing the full truth table of assignments against the values of the denoted sentences, highlighting the models, and marking the sceptical (least) and credulous (greatest) extensions when the tangle is positive. Finally it issues a conservativity verdict with an explanation: which structural theorem applies, how many admissible self-descriptions remain, and — when solvability fails — that the theory has become inconsistent. Users can discover for themselves that an even number of negations around a loop is harmless, that the tautological loop is conservative although nothing stratifies it, and that the liar is the unique failure mode.

Build a self-referential truth predicate and watch what it costs. Each name p, q, r denotes a sentence; the theory asserts Tp ↔ den(p) and so on. A model is a truth assignment to the names solving all the equations at once. Conservativity — adding no new theorem to the old theory — holds exactly when every base valuation admits a model.

1 · Denotations

Syntax: atom a, falsum F, truth atoms Tp Tq Tr, connectives ~ (not), &, |, ->, parentheses. Leave a box empty to remove that name from the tangle.

2 · Structural diagnosis

3 · Verdict

4 · The solution set, valuation by valuation

For each value of the base atom a we solve the loop equations by brute force. A row is a model when every equation Tc ↔ den(c) holds. The sceptical (least) and credulous (greatest) extensions are marked when the tangle is positive.

5 · What you are looking at

Positive — no truth atom sits under a negation. Then the revision operator R(w)(c) = ⟦den(c)⟧ is monotone, so by the Knaster–Tarski theorem it has a least and a greatest fixed point: a model always exists, however tangled the references.
Grounded — a rank on names strictly decreasing along every reference. Then there is exactly one model, whatever the polarities.
Locally stratified — negative references strictly descend in rank, positive ones may stay inside the level. This unifies the two conditions above: strange loops are allowed inside a level, and a model is built level by level.
The liar p ↦ ¬Tp satisfies none of them and has no model, so its theory is inconsistent — the one loop the mathematics refuses.

# Strange Loops, Priced Exactly *A guided tour of self-referential truth predicates: when they are free, when they cost a bit, and when they cost everything.* --- ## 1. The question Take a theory you trust — a set of statements in some ordinary vocabulary. Now bolt on a **tangled hierarchy**: a stock of *names* $c$, each of which denotes a sentence $\mathrm{den}(c)$, together with an internal truth predicate asserting, for each name, $$T c \;\longleftrightarrow\; \mathrm{den}(c).$$ The catch is that $\mathrm{den}(c)$ may itself mention $T c$, or $T d$ for a name $d$ whose sentence mentions $T c$. Reference may loop. This is Hofstadter's *strange loop*, stripped to its logical skeleton. The question is whether the old theory survives. Precisely: if $\psi$ is a sentence of the old, truth-free vocabulary, can the tangled theory prove $\psi$ when the old theory could not?
Why this is not obviously fine (click to expand) Self-reference has a bad reputation, earned by [the liar paradox](https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/liar-paradox/): the single name $c$ with $\mathrm{den}(c) = \neg T c$ produces the equation $w \leftrightarrow \neg w$, which has no solution. A theory with no models proves *everything*, including every old sentence you were still trying to decide. So one bad loop does not merely add noise — it destroys the host theory. [Tarski's undefinability theorem](https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/tarski-truth/) is usually read as an interdiction against languages containing their own truth predicate. The results below show that the interdiction is much narrower than it looks.
--- ## 2. Play first, theory later Before any definitions, build a tangle and see what happens. Type denotations for up to three names, or press a preset. The widget solves the loop equations by brute force, diagnoses the structural conditions, and issues a conservativity verdict. Try, in order: the **truth-teller** ($p \mapsto Tp$), the **liar** ($p \mapsto \neg Tp$), the **mutual loop** ($p \mapsto Tq$, $q \mapsto Tp$), and the **negative 2-cycle** ($p \mapsto \neg Tq$, $q \mapsto \neg Tp$). Watch the model count: $2$, $0$, $2$, $2$. Notice that the negative 2-cycle has models even though every link is a negation — an *even* number of negations around a loop is harmless. {{interactive_demo:0}} --- ## 3. The master key: conservativity *is* solvability Everything in this subject follows from one equivalence. > **Characterization of conservativity.** A tangled hierarchy adds no truth-free consequence to *any* truth-free base theory if and only if every valuation of the old atoms extends to an assignment of truth values to the names satisfying all the equations $T c \leftrightarrow \mathrm{den}(c)$.
The proof, in full — it is shorter than you expect **Solvable $\Rightarrow$ conservative.** Suppose the tangled theory entails the old sentence $\psi$, and let $v$ be any valuation of the old atoms satisfying the base theory $\mathcal{T}$. By hypothesis $v$ extends to a solution $w$ of the loop equations. The pair $(v,w)$ satisfies $\mathcal{T}$ — old sentences cannot see the truth predicate, so their value depends only on $v$ — and satisfies every biconditional. Hence it satisfies $\psi$; and since $\psi$ is old, $v$ alone satisfies $\psi$. So $\mathcal{T} \models \psi$. **Conservative $\Rightarrow$ solvable.** Suppose some valuation $v$ has no solution. Take as base theory the *diagram* of $v$: all old sentences true at $v$. Every model of the diagram has $v$'s atomic values, so the diagram plus the biconditionals has no model at all and entails $\bot$ — while the diagram alone is satisfied by $v$ and does not. Conservativity fails. $\blacksquare$
So the whole problem is: **when do the loop equations have a solution?** The next three sections answer it three ways. --- ## 4. Positivity: monotone loops are always solvable Call a formula **positive** when no truth atom sits under a negation (formally: under an even number of implication-antecedent positions). The key fact is monotonicity — making more names true can only make a positive formula truer. So the **revision operator** $$R(w)(c) \;=\; \text{value of } \mathrm{den}(c) \text{ when names are valued by } w$$ is a monotone map on the lattice of truth assignments, and [the Knaster–Tarski theorem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knaster%E2%80%93Tarski_theorem) hands us a least and a greatest fixed point for free. > **Positive tangles are conservative.** If every $\mathrm{den}(c)$ is positive, the loop equations are solvable over every base valuation — with *no* restriction on the reference graph, however tangled — and hence the tangle adds no old consequence to any old theory. The two fixed points have names. The **least** one is *sceptical*: assert a name true only when forced. The **greatest** is *credulous*: assert everything not forbidden. Every model lies between them, so all the indeterminacy of a positive tangle lives in that single interval — and the tangle determines its truth predicate exactly when the interval collapses to a point. {{algorithm:0}} --- ## 5. Grounding: descending references pin truth down The opposite discipline forbids loops instead of negations. A tangle is **grounded** when there is a rank $\mathrm{rk}$ on names with $\mathrm{rk}(c') < \mathrm{rk}(c)$ whenever $c'$ occurs in $\mathrm{den}(c)$: every reference points strictly downward. This is Tarski's own prescription, a hierarchy of metalanguages. > **Grounded tangles have exactly one model**, over every base valuation, whatever the polarities — hence they are conservative.
Construction and uniqueness Iterate the revision operator from the everywhere-false assignment. The value at a name of rank $n$ depends only on names of smaller rank, so it has stopped changing after $n+1$ steps; define $w(c)$ to be that stable value. Uniqueness is induction on rank: any two models agree at rank $0$ (those sentences mention no name), and agreeing below rank $n$ forces agreement at rank $n$.
The special case worth naming: if every name denotes an *old*, truth-free sentence, the biconditionals say exactly that the internal truth predicate is **sound and complete for the old language**. That is free — no new theorem, and not even a new degree of freedom, since the predicate is unique. --- ## 6. Local stratification: loops inside a level Positivity allows loops but no negation; grounding allows negation but no loops. The common generalization relaxes each restriction exactly where the other was strong. Track polarity *per name*: $c'$ occurs positively or negatively in $\mathrm{den}(c)$ according to the parity of antecedent positions above it. Then: > **Local stratification.** There is a rank with > - $\mathrm{rk}(c') < \mathrm{rk}(c)$ for every **negative** occurrence of $c'$ in $\mathrm{den}(c)$; > - $\mathrm{rk}(c') \le \mathrm{rk}(c)$ for every **positive** occurrence. > > **Every locally stratified tangle has a model, hence is conservative.** Strange loops may sit anywhere *inside* a level; only refutation-like dependencies must descend.
How the model is built (the prettiest construction in the subject) Process levels in increasing order. When building level $n$, freeze every name of rank $< n$ at the value already computed — legitimate precisely because negative dependencies point strictly down, so the frozen part enters with a fixed value — and take the *least fixed point* of the resulting operator on the names of level $n$, which is monotone because everything unfrozen occurs positively. A stability argument shows later levels never disturb earlier ones, so the levels glue into a single model. This is exactly why practitioners of [stratified negation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stratification_(mathematics)#Stratified_negation) in deductive databases and logic programming insist that recursion not pass through negation: it is this theorem that their discipline is buying.
Run the construction yourself: {{algorithm:2}} Deciding whether a given tangle admits such a rank is a shortest-path problem — a difference-constraint system whose only obstruction is a negative edge sitting on a cycle: {{algorithm:1}}
Two examples that mark the boundary exactly **Strictly more general.** Let $\mathrm{den}(q) = \bot$ and $\mathrm{den}(p) = Tq \to Tp$. Here $p$ has a positive self-loop (so no rank strictly descends) and $q$ occurs negatively (so the tangle is not positive). But $\mathrm{rk}(q)=0$, $\mathrm{rk}(p)=1$ locally stratifies it. Neither earlier theorem applies; the new one does. **Not necessary.** Let $\mathrm{den}(c) = Tc \to Tc$. The name occurs both positively and negatively in its own sentence, so no rank works — yet the sentence is a tautology and *every* assignment is a model, so the tangle is conservative. The exact criterion remains solvability; local stratification is merely a cheap sufficient test.
--- ## 7. Height collapse: infinitely tall, never transfinitely tall Drop numbers entirely and require only that the dependency relation be **well-founded** — no infinite descending chain of references. Truth is then definable by recursion along that order, uniquely, and conservativity follows. But something unexpected happens: > **Height collapse.** A tangle has a well-founded dependency relation **if and only if** it admits a rank function into the natural numbers with strictly descending references. The reason is that formulas are finite: the rank "one more than the maximum over the finitely many names I mention" is well defined, and lands in $\mathbb{N}$. A tangle can be *infinitely tall* — ranks unbounded — but no name ever lives at level $\omega$.
An infinite tower that is nowhere positive and still perfectly determined Take names $0, 1, 2, \dots$ plus one extra name $\star$, with $$\mathrm{den}(0) = \bot, \qquad \mathrm{den}(n+1) = \neg T n, \qquad \mathrm{den}(\star) = T0 .$$ Every link is a negation, so no positivity anywhere; the levels are unbounded, so no finite ceiling. It is nevertheless well-founded, hence conservative, and its truth predicate is *completely determined*: false, true, false, true, … all the way up, with $T\star$ false. **Infinite regress is not vicious circularity.**
--- ## 8. What a loop actually costs Conservativity says the tangle adds no *theorems*. It does not say it adds nothing. What it adds is **indeterminacy**, and the price list is exact. > **The cost of one loop.** For a single name: a grounded denotation ($\mathrm{den}(c) = \bot$) has exactly **one** model; a positive self-loop, the truth-teller ($\mathrm{den}(c) = Tc$), exactly **two**; a negative self-loop, the liar ($\mathrm{den}(c) = \neg Tc$), exactly **none**. > **$k$ loops.** The tangle of $k$ independent truth-tellers has exactly $2^k$ models, leaves each $Tc_i$ undecided, and *still* adds no truth-free consequence whatsoever. The slogan: **exponential in semantics, zero in syntax.** {{visualization:0}} And the correlation between negative self-reference and the loss of a model is not anecdotal. Enumerating every self-referential sentence of small depth over one atom, one name, and solving the loop equation for both base valuations, gives a complete census — in which *no* positive sentence ever loses a model: {{visualization:1}} --- ## 9. See the theorems run The full demonstration suite reproduces every quantitative claim above: the trichotomy $1/2/0$, the $2^k$ count, the sceptical/credulous interval and the determinacy criterion, the level-by-level construction, the infinite tower, the exhaustive census, and a brute-force audit comparing old and tangled entailment over a finite base language. {{demo:0}} The audit deserves its own reading. It compares entailment pairwise, in the old language and in the tangled one, and finds *zero* discrepancies for every conservative tangle and a flood of them for the liar: {{demo:1}} Deciding conservativity directly, by the criterion rather than by searching for proofs, is a satisfiability question — and this is what makes the structural conditions valuable, since they replace an exponential search by a linear-time construction: {{algorithm:3}} --- ## 10. What to take away | Condition on the tangle | Models per valuation | Conservative? | |---|---|---| | Arbitrary | — | iff every valuation expands to a model | | Positive (no truth atom negated) | $\ge 1$ | yes | | Grounded ($\mathbb{N}$-rank, all edges descend) | exactly $1$ | yes | | Locally stratified | $\ge 1$ | yes | | Well-founded dependency | exactly $1$ | yes | | $k$ independent truth-tellers | exactly $2^k$ | yes | | Single name: $\bot$ / $Tc$ / $\neg Tc$ | $1$ / $2$ / $0$ | yes / yes / **no** | Hofstadter's claim — that a strange loop does not corrupt the levels above it — turns out to be a theorem, with the fine print made explicit: **the loop is free provided its negations are grounded.** A system may represent itself, reason about its own representations, and close the circle, without changing a single fact about the world it models. What it pays is that some statements about itself are simply not determined: with $k$ independent loops it has $2^k$ equally admissible self-descriptions and no way to choose. And the one thing the mathematics refuses is the loop that turns back on itself in denial.

/-
# Conservativity for Tangled Hierarchies

A formal counterpart of Hofstadter's claim that *strange loops do not corrupt the
levels they sit above*.

We work with a propositional language `Frm α ι` whose atoms are indexed by `α`
and which contains, besides `⊥` and `→`, a family of **internal truth atoms**
`tr c` for `c : ι`.  A *tangled hierarchy* is a denotation function
`den : ι → Frm α ι`: the name `c` denotes the sentence `den c`, and `den c` is
allowed to mention `tr c` itself (a self-loop) or to run around an arbitrarily
long cycle of names.  The associated theory is the set of Tarski biconditionals
`tr c ↔ den c`.

Main results.

* `conservative_of_exists_model`: a tangled extension of a truth-free base theory
  is conservative as soon as every valuation of the old atoms extends to a model
  of the tangle.
* `conseq_tarski_iff_of_positive` (**Conservativity**): if every loop of the
  tangle is *positive* (each `den c` has all its truth atoms in positive
  position), then for every base theory `T` of truth-free sentences and every
  truth-free `ψ`, the tangled extension `T ∪ tarskiAx den` entails `ψ` iff `T`
  does.  The strange loops cost the old theory *nothing*.
* `stratified_conservative` (**Grounded hierarchies**): the same conclusion for
  arbitrary polarity as soon as the dependency relation of the tangle is bounded
  by a rank function (Tarski's stratification), together with
  `stratified_existsUnique_model`: there the internal truth predicate is
  *uniquely* determined.
* `liar_not_conservative` (**Sharpness**): the negative self-loop (the liar)
  destroys conservativity outright — the tangled theory becomes inconsistent.
* `selfLoop_model_ncard_trichotomy` (**The cost of one loop**): for a single
  name, a grounded denotation has exactly one model, a positive self-loop
  exactly two, and a negative self-loop none.
-/
import Mathlib

namespace TangledHierarchy

universe u v

variable {α : Type u} {ι : Type v}

/-! ## Syntax -/

/-- Propositional formulas with atoms from `α` and internal truth atoms from `ι`. -/
inductive Frm (α : Type u) (ι : Type v) where
  | atom : α → Frm α ι
  | fls : Frm α ι
  | imp : Frm α ι → Frm α ι → Frm α ι
  | tr : ι → Frm α ι

/-- Negation. -/
def fnot (φ : Frm α ι) : Frm α ι := Frm.imp φ Frm.fls

/-- Biconditional, encoded with `→` and `⊥`. -/
def fiff (φ ψ : Frm α ι) : Frm α ι :=
  fnot (Frm.imp (Frm.imp φ ψ) (fnot (Frm.imp ψ φ)))

/-- Truth-value of a formula under an atomic valuation `v` and an assignment `w`
of truth values to the names. -/
def eval (v : α → Prop) (w : ι → Prop) : Frm α ι → Prop
  | .atom a => v a
  | .fls => False
  | .imp φ ψ => eval v w φ → eval v w ψ
  | .tr c => w c

/-- Formulas not mentioning the internal truth predicate: the *old* language. -/
def TrFree : Frm α ι → Prop
  | .atom _ => True
  | .fls => True
  | .imp φ ψ => TrFree φ ∧ TrFree ψ
  | .tr _ => False

/-- `Occurs c φ`: the name `c` occurs in `φ`. -/
def Occurs (c : ι) : Frm α ι → Prop
  | .atom _ => False
  | .fls => False
  | .imp φ ψ => Occurs c φ ∨ Occurs c ψ
  | .tr c' => c' = c

/-- `Polar true φ` : every truth atom of `φ` occurs positively;
`Polar false φ` : every truth atom of `φ` occurs negatively. -/
def Polar : Bool → Frm α ι → Prop
  | _, .atom _ => True
  | _, .fls => True
  | b, .imp φ ψ => Polar (!b) φ ∧ Polar b ψ
  | b, .tr _ => b = true

/-! ## Semantics of the tangle -/

/-- A model of the tangled hierarchy: the truth assignment `w` obeys every
Tarski biconditional `w c ↔ eval (den c)`. -/
def TangleModel (den : ι → Frm α ι) (v : α → Prop) (w : ι → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ c, w c ↔ eval v w (den c)

/-- The theory of Tarski biconditionals attached to a tangled hierarchy. -/
def tarskiAx (den : ι → Frm α ι) : Set (Frm α ι) :=
  {φ | ∃ c, φ = fiff (Frm.tr c) (den c)}

/-- Satisfaction of a set of formulas. -/
def Sat (v : α → Prop) (w : ι → Prop) (T : Set (Frm α ι)) : Prop :=
  ∀ φ ∈ T, eval v w φ

/-- Semantic consequence. -/
def Conseq (T : Set (Frm α ι)) (ψ : Frm α ι) : Prop :=
  ∀ v w, Sat v w T → eval v w ψ

/-! ## Basic lemmas -/

@[simp] lemma eval_fnot (v : α → Prop) (w : ι → Prop) (φ : Frm α ι) :
    eval v w (fnot φ) ↔ ¬ eval v w φ := by
  simp [fnot, eval]

@[simp] lemma eval_fiff (v : α → Prop) (w : ι → Prop) (φ ψ : Frm α ι) :
    eval v w (fiff φ ψ) ↔ (eval v w φ ↔ eval v w ψ) := by
  simp only [fiff, eval_fnot, eval]
  tauto

lemma sat_tarskiAx_iff (den : ι → Frm α ι) (v : α → Prop) (w : ι → Prop) :
    Sat v w (tarskiAx den) ↔ TangleModel den v w := by
  constructor
  · intro h c
    have := h _ ⟨c, rfl⟩
    simpa [eval] using this
  · rintro h φ ⟨c, rfl⟩
    simpa [eval] using h c

/-- Truth-free formulas do not see the internal truth assignment. -/
lemma eval_congr_of_trFree (v : α → Prop) (w w' : ι → Prop) :
    ∀ {φ : Frm α ι}, TrFree φ → (eval v w φ ↔ eval v w' φ) := by
  intro φ
  induction φ with
  | atom a => intro _; rfl
  | fls => intro _; rfl
  | imp φ ψ ihφ ihψ =>
      rintro ⟨hφ, hψ⟩
      simp only [eval]
      rw [ihφ hφ, ihψ hψ]
  | tr c => intro h; exact absurd h (by simp [TrFree])

/-- Formulas agree under assignments that agree on the occurring names. -/
lemma eval_congr_of_occurs (v : α → Prop) (w w' : ι → Prop) :
    ∀ {φ : Frm α ι}, (∀ c, Occurs c φ → (w c ↔ w' c)) → (eval v w φ ↔ eval v w' φ) := by
  intro φ
  induction φ with
  | atom a => intro _; rfl
  | fls => intro _; rfl
  | imp φ ψ ihφ ihψ =>
      intro h
      simp only [eval]
      rw [ihφ fun c hc => h c (Or.inl hc), ihψ fun c hc => h c (Or.inr hc)]
  | tr c => intro h; exact h c rfl

/-- Monotonicity/antitonicity of evaluation according to polarity. -/
lemma eval_polar (v : α → Prop) {w w' : ι → Prop} (hw : ∀ c, w c → w' c) :
    ∀ (φ : Frm α ι),
      (Polar true φ → eval v w φ → eval v w' φ) ∧
      (Polar false φ → eval v w' φ → eval v w φ) := by
  intro φ
  induction φ with
  | atom a => exact ⟨fun _ h => h, fun _ h => h⟩
  | fls => exact ⟨fun _ h => h, fun _ h => h⟩
  | imp φ ψ ihφ ihψ =>
      refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
      · rintro ⟨hφ, hψ⟩ h hx
        exact ihψ.1 hψ (h (ihφ.2 (by simpa using hφ) hx))
      · rintro ⟨hφ, hψ⟩ h hx
        exact ihψ.2 hψ (h (ihφ.1 (by simpa using hφ) hx))
  | tr c =>
      refine ⟨fun _ h => hw c h, ?_⟩
      intro h; exact absurd h (by simp [Polar])

/-! ## The abstract conservativity criterion -/

/-- **Conservativity criterion.**  If every valuation of the old atoms extends to
a model of the tangle, the tangled theory has exactly the old truth-free
consequences. -/
theorem conservative_of_exists_model (den : ι → Frm α ι)
    (hex : ∀ v : α → Prop, ∃ w, TangleModel den v w)
    (T : Set (Frm α ι)) (hT : ∀ φ ∈ T, TrFree φ) (ψ : Frm α ι) (hψ : TrFree ψ) :
    Conseq (T ∪ tarskiAx den) ψ ↔ Conseq T ψ := by
  constructor
  · intro h v w hTw
    obtain ⟨w', hw'⟩ := hex v
    have hSat : Sat v w' (T ∪ tarskiAx den) := by
      rintro φ (hφ | hφ)
      · exact (eval_congr_of_trFree v w w' (hT φ hφ)).1 (hTw φ hφ)
      · exact ((sat_tarskiAx_iff den v w').2 hw') φ hφ
    exact (eval_congr_of_trFree v w' w hψ).1 (h v w' hSat)
  · intro h v w hTw
    exact h v w fun φ hφ => hTw φ (Or.inl hφ)

/-- Evaluation only depends on the atomic valuation up to pointwise equivalence. -/
lemma eval_congr_of_atoms (v v' : α → Prop) (w : ι → Prop) (h : ∀ a, v a ↔ v' a) :
    ∀ φ : Frm α ι, eval v w φ ↔ eval v' w φ := by
  intro φ
  induction φ with
  | atom a => exact h a
  | fls => rfl
  | imp φ ψ ihφ ihψ => simp only [eval]; rw [ihφ, ihψ]
  | tr c => rfl

/-- The truth-free diagram of a valuation. -/
def diagram (v : α → Prop) : Set (Frm α ι) :=
  {φ | TrFree φ ∧ eval v (fun _ => False) φ}

lemma diagram_trFree (v : α → Prop) : ∀ φ ∈ (diagram v : Set (Frm α ι)), TrFree φ :=
  fun _ h => h.1

lemma sat_diagram (v : α → Prop) (w : ι → Prop) : Sat v w (diagram (ι := ι) v) :=
  fun _ hφ => (eval_congr_of_trFree v (fun _ => False) w hφ.1).1 hφ.2

/-- Any model of the diagram of `v` has the same atomic valuation as `v`. -/
lemma atoms_of_sat_diagram {v v' : α → Prop} {w : ι → Prop}
    (h : Sat v' w (diagram (ι := ι) v)) (a : α) : v a ↔ v' a := by
  by_cases ha : v a
  · have : eval v' w (Frm.atom a : Frm α ι) :=
      h _ ⟨by simp [TrFree], by simpa [eval] using ha⟩
    simpa [eval, ha] using this
  · have : eval v' w (fnot (Frm.atom a) : Frm α ι) :=
      h _ ⟨by simp [TrFree, fnot], by simpa [eval] using ha⟩
    simp only [eval_fnot, eval] at this
    simp [ha, this]

/-- **Characterization of conservativity.**  A tangled hierarchy is conservative
over *every* truth-free base theory precisely when every valuation of the old
atoms can be expanded to a model of the tangle.  So conservativity is exactly
the solvability of the loop equations. -/
theorem conservative_iff_exists_model (den : ι → Frm α ι) :
    (∀ v : α → Prop, ∃ w, TangleModel den v w) ↔
      (∀ T : Set (Frm α ι), (∀ φ ∈ T, TrFree φ) → ∀ ψ : Frm α ι, TrFree ψ →
        (Conseq (T ∪ tarskiAx den) ψ ↔ Conseq T ψ)) := by
  constructor
  · intro hex T hT ψ hψ
    exact conservative_of_exists_model den hex T hT ψ hψ
  · intro h v
    by_contra hno
    push_neg at hno
    have hcons : Conseq ((diagram (ι := ι) v) ∪ tarskiAx den) Frm.fls := by
      intro v' w' hSat
      have hv : ∀ a, v a ↔ v' a :=
        atoms_of_sat_diagram (fun φ hφ => hSat φ (Or.inl hφ))
      have hmod : TangleModel den v' w' :=
        (sat_tarskiAx_iff den v' w').1 fun φ hφ => hSat φ (Or.inr hφ)
      have hmodv : TangleModel den v w' := by
        intro c
        rw [hmod c]
        exact (eval_congr_of_atoms v v' w' hv (den c)).symm
      exact absurd hmodv (hno w')
    have := (h (diagram v) (diagram_trFree v) Frm.fls (by simp [TrFree])).1 hcons
    have hfls := this v (fun _ => False) (sat_diagram v _)
    simp [eval] at hfls

/-! ## Existence of models for positive tangles (Knaster–Tarski) -/

/-- The one-step "truth revision" operator of a positive tangle, as a monotone map. -/
def revise (den : ι → Frm α ι) (hpos : ∀ c, Polar true (den c)) (v : α → Prop) :
    (ι → Prop) →o (ι → Prop) where
  toFun w := fun c => eval v w (den c)
  monotone' := by
    intro w w' hww c
    exact fun h => (eval_polar v (fun d hd => hww d hd) (den c)).1 (hpos c) h

/-- **Every positive tangled hierarchy has a model**, over any valuation of the
old atoms: the least fixed point of the revision operator. -/
theorem exists_tangleModel_of_positive (den : ι → Frm α ι)
    (hpos : ∀ c, Polar true (den c)) (v : α → Prop) :
    ∃ w, TangleModel den v w := by
  refine ⟨OrderHom.lfp (revise den hpos v), ?_⟩
  intro c
  have h := OrderHom.map_lfp (revise den hpos v)
  have hc := congrFun h c
  exact (iff_of_eq hc).symm

/-- **Conservativity for positive tangled hierarchies.**  Adding all Tarski
biconditionals of an arbitrary positively-looped tangle to a truth-free base
theory produces no new truth-free consequences: the strange loops are free. -/
theorem conseq_tarski_iff_of_positive (den : ι → Frm α ι)
    (hpos : ∀ c, Polar true (den c)) (T : Set (Frm α ι)) (hT : ∀ φ ∈ T, TrFree φ)
    (ψ : Frm α ι) (hψ : TrFree ψ) :
    Conseq (T ∪ tarskiAx den) ψ ↔ Conseq T ψ :=
  conservative_of_exists_model den (exists_tangleModel_of_positive den hpos) T hT ψ hψ

/-- Corollary: a truth-free base theory stays consistent after tangling, as long
as the tangle is positive. -/
theorem consistent_of_positive (den : ι → Frm α ι) (hpos : ∀ c, Polar true (den c))
    (T : Set (Frm α ι)) (hT : ∀ φ ∈ T, TrFree φ)
    (hcon : ¬ Conseq T (Frm.fls : Frm α ι)) :
    ¬ Conseq (T ∪ tarskiAx den) (Frm.fls : Frm α ι) := fun h =>
  hcon ((conseq_tarski_iff_of_positive den hpos T hT Frm.fls (by simp [TrFree])).1 h)

/-! ## Grounded (stratified) hierarchies: existence *and* uniqueness -/

/-- The revision sequence started from the empty extension. -/
def reviseIter (den : ι → Frm α ι) (v : α → Prop) : ℕ → (ι → Prop)
  | 0 => fun _ => False
  | n + 1 => fun c => eval v (reviseIter den v n) (den c)

section Stratified

variable (den : ι → Frm α ι) (rk : ι → ℕ)
  (hrk : ∀ c c', Occurs c' (den c) → rk c' < rk c) (v : α → Prop)

include hrk in
/-- In a stratified tangle the revision sequence is stable strictly above the rank. -/
lemma reviseIter_stable :
    ∀ n, ∀ c, rk c < n → ∀ m, rk c < m →
      (reviseIter den v n c ↔ reviseIter den v m c) := by
  intro n
  induction n using Nat.strong_induction_on with
  | _ n ih =>
    intro c hcn m hcm
    match n, m with
    | 0, _ => exact absurd hcn (by omega)
    | n + 1, 0 => exact absurd hcm (by omega)
    | n + 1, m + 1 =>
        simp only [reviseIter]
        refine eval_congr_of_occurs v _ _ ?_
        intro c' hc'
        have hlt : rk c' < rk c := hrk c c' hc'
        exact ih n (by omega) c' (by omega) m (by omega)

/-- The canonical truth assignment of a stratified tangle. -/
def stratModel : ι → Prop := fun c => reviseIter den v (rk c + 1) c

include hrk in
lemma stratModel_isModel : TangleModel den v (stratModel den rk v) := by
  intro c
  have h1 : stratModel den rk v c ↔ eval v (reviseIter den v (rk c)) (den c) := by
    simp [stratModel, reviseIter]
  rw [h1]
  refine eval_congr_of_occurs v _ _ ?_ |>.symm
  intro c' hc'
  have hlt : rk c' < rk c := hrk c c' hc'
  have := reviseIter_stable den rk hrk v (rk c' + 1) c' (by omega) (rk c) (by omega)
  simpa [stratModel] using this

include hrk in
/-- **Stratified tangles have a unique model.** -/
theorem stratified_existsUnique_model : ∃! w, TangleModel den v w := by
  refine ⟨stratModel den rk v, stratModel_isModel den rk hrk v, ?_⟩
  intro w hw
  have key : ∀ n, ∀ c, rk c ≤ n → (w c ↔ stratModel den rk v c) := by
    intro n
    induction n using Nat.strong_induction_on with
    | _ n ih =>
      intro c hcn
      have hm := stratModel_isModel den rk hrk v c
      rw [hw c, hm]
      refine eval_congr_of_occurs v _ _ ?_
      intro c' hc'
      have hlt : rk c' < rk c := hrk c c' hc'
      exact ih (rk c') (by omega) c' le_rfl
  funext c
  exact propext (key (rk c) c le_rfl)

include hrk in
/-- **Conservativity for grounded hierarchies**, with no positivity assumption:
a level-respecting tangle adds nothing to the old theory. -/
theorem stratified_conservative (T : Set (Frm α ι)) (hT : ∀ φ ∈ T, TrFree φ)
    (ψ : Frm α ι) (hψ : TrFree ψ) :
    Conseq (T ∪ tarskiAx den) ψ ↔ Conseq T ψ :=
  conservative_of_exists_model den
    (fun v => ⟨stratModel den rk v, stratModel_isModel den rk hrk v⟩) T hT ψ hψ

end Stratified

/-! ## Internal soundness for the old theory costs nothing -/

lemma trFree_not_occurs : ∀ {φ : Frm α ι}, TrFree φ → ∀ c, ¬ Occurs c φ := by
  intro φ
  induction φ with
  | atom a => intro _ c h; exact h
  | fls => intro _ c h; exact h
  | imp φ ψ ihφ ihψ =>
      rintro ⟨hφ, hψ⟩ c (h | h)
      · exact ihφ hφ c h
      · exact ihψ hψ c h
  | tr c' => intro h; exact absurd h (by simp [TrFree])

/-- A *naming of the old theory*: every name denotes a truth-free sentence.  The
associated Tarski biconditionals are exactly the internal soundness (and
completeness) statements for the old language. -/
theorem groundedNaming_conservative (den : ι → Frm α ι) (hden : ∀ c, TrFree (den c))
    (T : Set (Frm α ι)) (hT : ∀ φ ∈ T, TrFree φ) (ψ : Frm α ι) (hψ : TrFree ψ) :
    Conseq (T ∪ tarskiAx den) ψ ↔ Conseq T ψ :=
  stratified_conservative den (fun _ => 0)
    (fun c c' h => absurd h (trFree_not_occurs (hden c) c')) T hT ψ hψ

/-- Moreover the internal truth predicate of such a naming is uniquely
determined: adding internal soundness for the old theory costs neither a new
theorem nor a new degree of freedom. -/
theorem groundedNaming_unique (den : ι → Frm α ι) (hden : ∀ c, TrFree (den c))
    (v : α → Prop) : ∃! w, TangleModel den v w :=
  stratified_existsUnique_model den (fun _ => 0)
    (fun c c' h => absurd h (trFree_not_occurs (hden c) c')) v

/-! ## Sharpness: the liar loop is not conservative -/

/-- The liar tangle on a single name. -/
def liarDen : Unit → Frm Unit Unit := fun _ => fnot (Frm.tr ())

theorem liar_no_model (v : Unit → Prop) : ¬ ∃ w, TangleModel liarDen v w := by
  rintro ⟨w, hw⟩
  have h := hw ()
  simp only [liarDen, eval_fnot, eval] at h
  tauto

/-- **The negative self-loop destroys conservativity**: the tangled theory over
the empty base theory is inconsistent, while the empty theory is not. -/
theorem liar_not_conservative :
    Conseq ((∅ : Set (Frm Unit Unit)) ∪ tarskiAx liarDen) Frm.fls ∧
      ¬ Conseq (∅ : Set (Frm Unit Unit)) Frm.fls := by
  constructor
  · intro v w hSat
    refine absurd ⟨w, ?_⟩ (liar_no_model v)
    exact (sat_tarskiAx_iff liarDen v w).1 fun φ hφ => hSat φ (Or.inr hφ)
  · intro h
    have := h (fun _ => True) (fun _ => True) (by intro φ hφ; exact absurd hφ (by simp))
    simp [eval] at this

/-! ## The cost of one loop -/

/-- The truth-teller tangle on a single name. -/
def tellerDen : Unit → Frm Unit Unit := fun _ => Frm.tr ()

/-- A grounded denotation on a single name. -/
def groundedDen : Unit → Frm Unit Unit := fun _ => Frm.fls

lemma unit_fun_eq {w : Unit → Prop} {p : Prop} (h : w () ↔ p) : w = fun _ => p := by
  funext u
  cases u
  exact propext h

/-- **The cost of one loop.**  With a single name: a grounded denotation pins the
truth predicate down (one model), a positive self-loop leaves it free (two
models), and a negative self-loop is contradictory (no models). -/
theorem selfLoop_model_ncard_trichotomy (v : Unit → Prop) :
    {w : Unit → Prop | TangleModel groundedDen v w}.ncard = 1 ∧
    {w : Unit → Prop | TangleModel tellerDen v w}.ncard = 2 ∧
    {w : Unit → Prop | TangleModel liarDen v w}.ncard = 0 := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · have hset : {w : Unit → Prop | TangleModel groundedDen v w} = {fun _ => False} := by
      ext w
      simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_singleton_iff, TangleModel]
      constructor
      · intro h
        exact unit_fun_eq (by simpa [groundedDen, eval] using h ())
      · rintro rfl c
        simp [groundedDen, eval]
    rw [hset, Set.ncard_singleton]
  · have hset : {w : Unit → Prop | TangleModel tellerDen v w}
        = {(fun _ => False), (fun _ => True)} := by
      ext w
      simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_insert_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff, TangleModel]
      constructor
      · intro _
        rcases Classical.em (w ()) with h | h
        · exact Or.inr (unit_fun_eq (by simp [h]))
        · exact Or.inl (unit_fun_eq (by simp [h]))
      · rintro (rfl | rfl) <;> intro c <;> simp [tellerDen, eval]
    rw [hset]
    refine Set.ncard_pair ?_
    intro h
    have := congrFun h ()
    simp at this
  · have hset : {w : Unit → Prop | TangleModel liarDen v w} = ∅ := by
      ext w
      simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_empty_iff_false, iff_false]
      exact fun h => liar_no_model v ⟨w, h⟩
    rw [hset, Set.ncard_empty]

/-- The positive self-loop leaves its own truth value undecided: neither it nor
its negation follows from the tangled theory. -/
theorem teller_undecided :
    ¬ Conseq (tarskiAx tellerDen) (Frm.tr ()) ∧
      ¬ Conseq (tarskiAx tellerDen) (fnot (Frm.tr ())) := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    have hmod : TangleModel tellerDen (fun _ => True) (fun _ => False) := by
      intro c; simp [tellerDen, eval]
    have := h (fun _ => True) (fun _ => False)
      ((sat_tarskiAx_iff tellerDen _ _).2 hmod)
    simp [eval] at this
  · intro h
    have hmod : TangleModel tellerDen (fun _ => True) (fun _ => True) := by
      intro c; simp [tellerDen, eval]
    have := h (fun _ => True) (fun _ => True)
      ((sat_tarskiAx_iff tellerDen _ _).2 hmod)
    simp [eval] at this

end TangledHierarchy
